extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of constitutional law, political theory, and comparative government; policymakers and historians
extracted.subtask_description: A list of criteria and considerations for judging the merits and defects of federal systems of government, illustrated by American experience (e.g., enforcement against recalcitrant states, uniformity of law, local self-government).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect on foreign relations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal character of a government may be an unfortunate influence on its foreign relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text argues that federal structure can weaken the national government's standing abroad; example: the doctrine of State sovereignty and secession in 1861 gave European powers plausible grounds to treat insurgents as belligerents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to enforce national authority against a State
rubrics_metrics.description: How readily the central government can enforce its will against a single State or disobedient subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical examples (Jackson 1832, Kansas troubles 1855–56, Grant's reconquest of southern States) show occasional weakness; while Civil War prestige and improved communications strengthen enforcement, States still enjoy legal and local-sentiment advantages that enable resistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk and legal basis of secession
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the constitutional and political order permits secession or makes it plausible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The doctrine of State sovereignty grounded in federalism helped precipitate the 1861 secession; although now less probable and legally 'indestructible', establishing that security cost immense lives and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tendency of States to combine into blocs
rubrics_metrics.description: The propensity for States to form regional groups acting together in opposition to national interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Past examples: South Carolina/Gulf States, New England. National parties have made official State combinations less fashionable, and using State revenues/machinery for common disloyal purposes is now less probable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity to regulate corporations and effect social reforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether federal authority can effectively regulate powerful incorporated companies and enact nation‑wide social reforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late-19th-century pressures highlighted limits: Congress was seen as limited to interstate commerce, leaving corporate creation/management to States; demands for federal action on child labour and other reforms spurred calls for constitutional amendment or new judicial constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniformity in private law and administration
rubrics_metrics.description: The degree of uniformity (or diversity) in private law (marriage, divorce, contracts, torts, commercial law) and administrative methods across States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some diversity is valuable (social/cultural variety), but differences in coinage, weights, commercial rules are inconvenient; divorce laws show significant divergences and abuses; States have appointed Commissions to seek uniform legislation where desirable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complexity of governmental machinery vs smoothness of operation
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether an elaborate, interlaced system of authorities leads to breakdowns or, with familiarization, to smooth working.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although intricate mechanisms might seem prone to deadlocks and expense, familiarity with the system and distribution of functions can secure smooth operation; expense is considered acceptable compared with risks from untrustworthy centralized officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate selection motivated by State interest rather than merit
rubrics_metrics.description: The practice of selecting federal office candidates based on the effect of their nomination on the State's vote rather than the candidate's intrinsic merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This can lead to second-rate men running for high office to carry a State, favor politicians from large States, and constrain presidential Cabinet choices (e.g., avoiding two persons from same State).

rubrics_metrics.name: Federalism's role in intensifying sectional parties and conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent to which federal arrangements encourage parties and controversies tied to State identities and legal differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the slavery struggle, federalism caused parties to become identified with States, produced legal controversies over state law differences, damaged the Supreme Court's credit by perceptions of partiality, and contributed to secession and civil war; federalism shaped the particular form of the conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance between powers left to States and national authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether leaving particular powers with States produces dangerous political controversy and impedes national assertion, or whether it averts wider discord.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federalism inherently leaves certain powers to States which may create uniquely dangerous controversies; against this are advantages that diversity can avert or localize discord that might otherwise become national.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity to unite separate commonwealths without extinguishing local administrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Federalism's ability to form one nation under a national government while preserving separate administrations, legislatures, and local patriotisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This was a primary reason for adopting federalism (U.S. 1787; parallels in German Empire, suggestions for Ireland/colonies); it's a distinguishing advantage when full fusion is undesirable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for developing new and vast territories
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent to which federal arrangements permit expansion and development adapted to local conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federalism allows variety of methods, legal adaptation, and self-reliance in new regions; laws and remedies can be tailored to local economic needs, aiding natural growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevention of despotic central government and protection of liberties
rubrics_metrics.description: The degree to which federal structures check the concentration of power and guard private liberties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal distribution of power was designed to prevent central despotism; even if fears now appear idle, the principle remains as a bulwark often invoked by States against central encroachment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civic education and stimulation from local self-government
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether local self-government stimulates popular interest in neighbourhood affairs and educates citizens in civic duty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-government sustains local political life, teaches vigilance and sacrifices necessary for liberty and prosperity; but its benefits vary with the scale and character of the unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of local administration through resident oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: The effectiveness of local administration when inhabitants have means to oversee conduct of local business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local oversight secures better administration of local affairs; in some parts of the U.S. (cities, counties, townships, school districts) local self-government is more complete than in European countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to try legislative and administrative experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Federalism's capacity to let individual States try laws and administrative methods that can be copied or avoided by others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small commonwealths can make and unmake laws quickly; mistakes are less serious and successful experiments profit other States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compartmentalization of risks (diminishing national exposure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Federalism's ability to contain crises or discord within parts of the nation, preventing spread to the whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogy of a ship with water-tight compartments: local social or economic disorder may damage one State but leave the rest of the federation intact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relieving the national legislature of excessive burdens
rubrics_metrics.description: Division of powers reduces the mass of functions the central legislature must handle, improving focus and timeliness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numerous local legislatures handle diverse regional needs, enabling the national body to deliberate on matters of country-wide import without being swamped by local detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local fiscal control and oversight of public works
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal structure provides machinery for better control of taxes raised and spent in a region and oversight of public works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local governments are better positioned to monitor expenditure and projects in their area than a distant central authority; this is a concrete administrative benefit of federalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of State size and population for local self-government
rubrics_metrics.description: The utility of local self-government depends on the population and area of constituent units; very large States may erode local involvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1787 States were small enough for personal political knowledge; by 1907 many States were far larger, reducing personal stakes and limiting citizens' active political engagement; creating more (smaller) States might have preserved local benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency of elections and their educative effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether numerous and frequent elections educate citizens or overtax their attention and leave them vulnerable to party machines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While frequent elections can educate, excessive frequency 'overtaxes' attention, fritters interest, and may leave citizens at the mercy of knots of selfish adventurers and party chiefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical effectiveness of the division of legislative powers
rubrics_metrics.description: The division of legislative powers should be judged by how well it enables different levels of government to handle their proper share of affairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State legislatures relieve Congress of many demands; because of material diversity across the Union, a single central legislature could not easily pass measures suited to every region; the division thus improves practical governance.
